items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed in the post-review branch head 328f6bb11cfced33097ba209d57066fc3f085613 (carried into the merged commit cae8dcfaf1e54f9d0015b30150f3d3979b7e08b6): the read-layer filter now applies a raw lowercased-email expression to the not-in predicate, matching the other two layers.
items.description: Of the three defensive layers keeping shared ops-mailbox accounts out of the staff filter, the read-layer query filter compares raw email values case-sensitively while the database CHECK constraint and the backfill SQL both lowercase the email first. A row carrying a mixed-case ops mailbox address alongside a staff role therefore bypasses the read-layer filter and surfaces in the dropdown — exactly the pre-constraint or constraint-bypass scenario the adjacent comment claims this filter defends against.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed in the post-review branch head 328f6bb11cfced33097ba209d57066fc3f085613, where the comment cites the regenerated migration's real class name.
items.description: A code comment cross-references the migration that introduced the CHECK constraint by class name, but the cited name (a round timestamp ending in six zeros) does not match any migration file in the tree — the actual file's timestamp differs. A reader following the reference finds nothing.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed in the post-review branch head 328f6bb11cfced33097ba209d57066fc3f085613: all four sites read the first row via optional chaining instead of the non-null assertion.
items.description: The backfill integration test uses the non-null assertion operator at four assertion sites when reading the role off the first row of a query result, which the repository's TypeScript style rule bans outright. A length-check guard or optional chaining preserves the assertion intent while narrowing safely.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed in the post-review branch head 328f6bb11cfced33097ba209d57066fc3f085613: the round-stamped file is gone and its contents were regenerated as migration files carrying natural generated timestamps.
items.description: The migration's class name carries a hand-rounded two-a.m. timestamp rather than a generated one — the fingerprint of a hand-authored migration, which the repository's instruction file forbids: migrations must be produced through the generator command. The overwhelming majority of sibling migrations carry natural generated timestamps, and the file should be regenerated with its body copied over.
